findings: Naming: script.md, storyboard.md, production-notes.md and brief.md name no employer. A grep for common employer and vendor names found none. The only third-party names are the ones the spec's closed claim list allows: Sentia (C10), Cloudflare AI Gateway and GitHub (C8), and Apache 2.0 (C9).
No other factory, product, video or person is named or referenced. production-notes.md cites the Sentia repository arananet/sentia only as GLB provenance, which is first-party and not a spoken claim.
Spec S4 is met: script.md, storyboard.md and production-notes.md contain no em dash or en dash characters. I checked with a grep for U+2013 and U+2014.

Promises: the script makes only claims from the spec's closed list C1 to C11. The only counts are the three intake kinds (named without a count), five reviewers and five Sentia layers. Section 5 states five reviewers for the factory in general, so it does not tie the number to this video's own panel (flag F1). Section 7 says the content line wrote, rendered and reviewed the video and that it stopped at the human gate, and it claims no publication.

Search-ranking risk: the spoken address sentia.info-693.workers.dev is the only external link and matches C10. The script contains no superlatives, no 'first' or 'best' claims, no subscribe or call-to-action wording, and no comparison with other products.
Disclosure: production-notes.md records that the narration is synthetic speech and that the YouTube AI generated content label must be set at publish time. Nothing is published in this pass.
Scope: I judged naming and policy on the text inputs only. The finished film is not yet in the tree, so on-screen text in the rendered frames is for the second pass to re-confirm.
